QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah's Category I Venture Capital AIF is interested in a teaser received from an investee company. Before the investee's investment banker releases the Confidential Information Memorandum (CIM), what is the MOST critical document the fund must typically execute?

explanation.text: The Logic: The standard practice is: Teaser (no NDA) → interest shown → NDA signed → CIM/IM shared. The NDA is used extensively as a matter of convention to enable the investee company to share technical and financial confidential information safely. The Trap: Term sheet comes much later, after business DD and IC 'go-ahead'. SSA and SHA are definitive agreements executed at closing — long after CIM review. Proprietary-sourced deals may sign NDA directly with the target. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests the same NDA-before-CIM sequence. XIX-A Distributor exam does NOT cover investee-side NDAs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Push for a 'two-way' NDA: the investee protects its data, but you also protect your internal evaluation IP and prior investment thesis. Include a standstill clause so the company cannot approach your LPs during the NDA validity.
